# Implement block: Starfield Payment Success (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Starfield Payment Success" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A full-screen payment form on black with a maroon tint at the top and an orange light under the bottom edge: "Enter Amount", a large light amount ("0.00 USD" with a violet caret), a conversion chip, a grey card row ("**** 3256") and a number pad without key shapes. Typing an amount brings a violet "Confirm" pill up from the bottom while the pad's rows close up to make room. Confirm takes the form apart (the amount floats up, the card and the pad sink) and leaves a field of stars flying past, with "Starting your transaction" under a dark paper plane on a wobbling yellow light. Then a thin red ring bursts outward, a green check lands, swells, darkens and turns over, and what comes round is a spinning gold coin over "Successfully sent", the amount, and a "Review" pill with a round share button.

**Motion.** Keys flash a 72 pt circle (on in 40 ms, off in 350 ms) with a light haptic; a digit fades in over 140 ms and the caret blinks once a second, solid for its first half. Confirm rises 0.4 s after the last key on a spring (damping 17, stiffness 190, mass 1), and the same value moves the pad: its first row from 59 to 25 pt under the card and its rows from about 80 to 74 pt apart, so both overshoot a little; it leaves in 220 ms when the amount is deleted. On release one clock drives everything, in seconds. Confirm drops off the bottom edge in 0.28 (quadratic ease in). From 0.06 to 0.51 the amount floats up 140 pt and the card and the rows sink 100 pt, both quadratic, fading over the first 50–85% of that, with the tint and the orange light. Stars fade in from 0.4 to 1.0: 240 fixed stars at depths 0–1 around a point 36% down the screen, drawn at 1 / (0.18 + 0.82 z) of a far plane half the screen's height wide, radius 0.65 + 1.7 (1 − z)³ pt with a 2.2 pt blurred glow on the near ones, moving 0.05 of the depth a second towards the viewer. The text rises 26 pt and fades in from 0.5 to 0.85. The light condenses from 0.75 to 1.15 (scale 0.5 to 1): four yellow discs of about 27 pt (#FFC61C over an orange-red bloom, a pale core) wander ±0.4 rad and ±35% of 11 pt round the centre at 1.7–2.9 rad/s, the whole breathing 5% at 3.3 rad/s and bobbing 2.5 pt; the plane fades in from 1.0 to 1.25 and leans ±0.05 rad. After the wait (2.7 s) text and plane fade in 0.3; at +0.35 the check lands: an 87 pt disc (#1EE07A) scaling in over 0.5 s with a 10% overshoot (back out), two 1.5 pt rings (#E5432A) growing with a cubic ease out over 0.8 s to 42% and 92% of the screen's height while fading, the stars rushing 0.3 of the depth over 1 s, and a success haptic. At +0.55 Review slides up over 0.45 s (back out), the share button 70 ms behind. From +0.85 to +1.15 the check swells to 1.3 and darkens to #12964F, then turns about its vertical axis, easing over 0.3 s up to one turn every 1.3 s; at a quarter turn the 112 pt coin (14 pt edge, leaning 8°) takes its place edge-on and keeps turning: the face away from the light darkens by up to 66% and a band of light crosses it. The result's three lines rise 14 pt and fade in over 0.35 s from +1.45, 80 ms apart. Review, the share button or the close button fade the sky out over 0.36 s and bring the empty form back over 0.6 s, the pad's rows 28 pt from below and 36 ms apart. The self-playing demo types 1, 0, 0 at 0.8, 1.15 and 1.5 s, presses Confirm at 2.6 s for 0.15 s and leaves the result 3.6 s after the check, every 11 s, without haptics; a touch takes over and the loop starts again 3 s later, once the form is idle. Under reduced motion nothing travels: the form cross-fades, the stars stand still, the light does not wobble, there is no ring, and the check cross-fades to a coin that faces the viewer. Android 26–27 approximates the Gaussian star halos, wandering light, rings and coin glow with bounded weighted canvas layers; Android 28+ uses native blur masks.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [StarfieldPaymentSuccessDemo.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/starfieldpaymentsuccess/StarfieldPaymentSuccessDemo.kt)

### Files of the block

- [Space.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/starfieldpaymentsuccess/Space.kt)
- [StarfieldPaymentSuccess.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/starfieldpaymentsuccess/StarfieldPaymentSuccess.kt)

### Shared helpers the block uses

- [kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt)

### Libraries

It needs no library beyond a new Compose project.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
